Subject: Clarify: blended-unit accounting and minimums for Q1 pilot

Hi Sarah — great question, thanks for calling it out. Summary below plus a worked example attached.

Short answers:
- Token counting: we bill tokens consumed per request (prompt + generated tokens) across models. For retrieval-augmented calls the retrieval tokens are included in the prompt token count for that call.
- Minimums: our standard enterprise pilot uses a per-month commit (committed tokens). Usage is aggregated across all calls; we apply a monthly minimum (not per-request).
- Rounding/quantum: we meter tokens to the nearest 10-token quantum for billing (round up). Example: 143 tokens -> 150 billed.
- Discounts: discounts are applied to billed units after minimuming. If actual usage < committed minimum in a billing month we bill the committed minimum and apply the negotiated discount rate to that invoiced amount. For pilots we typically offer a one-time first-month shortfall credit — see below.

Worked example (attached as sample-invoice.pdf and pricing-matrix.xlsx):
- Actual usage in Month 1: 2,345 tokens
- Rounded billed usage (10-token quantum): 2,350 tokens
- Committed minimum: 50,000 tokens / month
- Invoiceable units: max(rounded usage, committed minimum) = 50,000 tokens
- List price per token (blended): $0.0004 -> gross = $20.00
- Negotiated discount: 25% -> invoice = $15.00
- One-time shortfall credit (pilot concession): if agreed, credit = committed-minimum - actual-charged difference prorated for first month; we can structure as a line-item credit.

Next steps: I've attached the sample invoice and our pricing matrix. If Acme confirms the one-time credit for month 1 we can include that in the SOW/DocuSign and show the updated invoice line. If you'd like I can loop in Finance for an explicit calc.

Regards,
Jordan Blake

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal alignment we can confirm the following for the pilot:

- Billing units: tokens are counted per request and rounded up to the 10-token quantum. Retrieval tokens included in prompt counts.
- Minimums and discounts: monthly committed minimum will be invoiced if actual rounded usage is below the commit. Discount (25%) applies to the invoiced amount (post-minimum).
- One-time credit: Redwood will issue a one-time "Pilot shortfall credit" for Month 1 equal to the delta between the committed minimum invoice and actual billed amount, capped at 30% of the committed-month invoice, reflected as a separate invoice line.

I've updated the SOW and included a DocuSign link: https://d.docs.redwood/p/SOW/ACME-2026 (attachment: sow-docusign-link.txt). I also attached a redlined SOW for your legal team.
